title: Local subprocess executor: start/inspect/cancel/collect over a worktree per attempt, runner claude|codex|pi
description:
internal/exec/subprocess: the four operations over JobSpec/JobHandle/JobStatus/JobResult (contracts/job-protocol.json). start: git worktree per attempt on branch tick/<id> from JobSpec.source_ref, runner launched headless (claude -p / codex exec / pi, full-auto flags), the worker prompt rendered from the tick and the RESULT path OWNED by the executor (absolute, inside the attempt worktree, JobSpec.artifact_prefix) so the worker cwd is irrelevant. inspect: pid liveness, worktree state, commits beyond the recorded base, RESULT presence and STATUS line — completion is DURABLE EVIDENCE ONLY, never process exit; settled-but-incomplete is a distinct status. cancel: revoke (kill process tree) before any teardown, idempotent. collect: read the branch, parse RESULT, boundary diff against the attempt base SHA restricted to tracker records (.tick/issues, .tick/activity; config.md, runners.toml, learnings.md exempt). Timer push of in-progress work to origin (Appendix A #5). Handle identity = (repo key, run, tick, attempt). Also expose the Unix-style JSON commands ticfac-exec-subprocess start|inspect|cancel|collect < json. REQUIRED TESTS (Peter, 2026-09-02): finished-worker detection with no lost-event race (worker settles while nobody inspects; next inspect sees it); a killed-and-re-issued wait sees settled work immediately; a worker that cds to /tmp then writes RESULT still collects; two repos with the same tick id concurrently do not collide; cleanup leaves zero run-created worktrees/branches; kill -9 of the executor mid-job leaves a reconcilable handle. Use a fake runner script for unit tests; one opt-in live test with a real claude or codex.

## How this fits
You own internal/exec/subprocess (plus cmd/ticfac-exec-subprocess for the JSON commands). Runner values claude|codex|pi; use a fake runner script in unit tests. The run-state store (xkd) and tk client (y7o) are being built concurrently — do not depend on them; the reconciler (next wave) wires everything together.

Integration branch epic/qeu already contains wave 1 (tick b6s, commit 38889bad1fd725a897bd1a4fd75ef41217d3acfa): Go module github.com/pengelbrecht/ticfac (stdlib-only, go 1.24), the vendored contract bundle 3.0.0 under contracts/ (NEVER edit it; go test refuses local edits), internal/schema (ParseSchema/ParseDefs/Validate — the validator to use for every bundle document; its refusal strings are contract surface), internal/contracts (Dir()/RepoRoot() locate the bundle from any test depth), and internal/contracts/parity with one reader per bundle file — including a test-scoped CAS fake (parity/cas_fake_test.go) and lifecycle harness (parity/lifecycle_harness_test.go) that your real implementation must agree with. Read README.md, CONTRACTS.md and the RESULT of wave 1 in git history (commit message of 9a3faa3) before starting. Three ticks run in parallel in this wave (qg5 executor, xkd run-state store, y7o tk client); stay inside your own package directory, do not touch go.mod (no third-party deps — stdlib only), README.md, or files owned by the other two. Verify your base: git merge-base --is-ancestor 38889bad1fd725a897bd1a4fd75ef41217d3acfa HEAD.
acceptance_criteria: Four operations pass the job-protocol goldens; the required tests above are green with a fake runner; the lifecycle-invariants suite passes against this executor for the invariants it covers; ticfac-exec-subprocess round-trips JSON on stdin/stdout; go test -short ./internal/exec/... green.
